analysis:
Reviewed the head text of scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (lines 875-1440), plus the patch and metadata for scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py. Both files are offline CI-structure unit tests. The PR touches no shipped provider code, coordinator protocol, attestation, key handling, cache storage or fan helper. The T-041 prefix-cache definition was supplied as context, but nothing in the diff touches those source files, so the TB-007 and A-001 cache-storage threats are unaffected.

The changed assertions track workflow changes made elsewhere in the PR: build jobs now run only when their lane runs, there is a tree-name record step, the warm workflow gains a cron schedule and no longer triggers on push to master or on scripts/**, and the DEV caller paths matching is loosened.

The visible tests keep CI hardening checks intact. Cache saves are gated on SAVE_CACHES for pushes to master only. Master uses a strict-cache tier. Checkouts use persist-credentials: false. Unsafe .git caches (hooks, fsmonitor, include, symlink) are discarded. Every cache step is gated off on a Darkbloom runner without a cache URL. No secrets or backend references appear in the provider job, and the composite action has no continue-on-error.

One minor point: test_the_cluster_runtime_scripts_start_the_release_lanes now checks the DEV caller with a looser substring match, '{script}' rather than the exact list-item line. This slightly weakens the test but is not a security regression.

The actual workflow YAML files (provider-plan.yml, warm workflow, callers) are not in this batch. Whether the warm workflow's trigger and gate changes are safe against PR cache poisoning or default-branch seeding depends on files outside the supplied evidence, so they need review elsewhere.
